main_text.l: time coactam, præsidibus & actionem dirigentibus iis, quibus id jus erat, summam rerum totius civitatis esse voluit Solon.

Ea ex Solonis lege de Senatus actis judicabat, leges veteres recognoscebat, novas, si res posceret, ferebat, bella jubebat ac finiebat, pacemque reficiebat, magistratus majores, archontes, belli duces, hipparchos, navarchos plurefque alios creabat, fœdera feriebat, legatos edebat,& quò vellet,cum mandatis mittebat, civitatem exteris dabat, bene meritis præmia constituebat, judicia etiam quædam exercebat talium criminum, de quibus certæ leges non erant scriptæ: cujusmodi fuit εἰσαγ-γελίας, cujus accusatus damnatusque est Alcibiades. In hanc concionem universus populus ex eadem Solonis lege coibat sine ullo classium discrimine, etiam ii, qui erant classis imæ, habebantque omnes par suffragii jus. Locus concionis communiter erat aut forum aut Pnyx prope arcem fori instar, interdum etiam amplissimum theatrum Bacchi: ordinarium tempus dies tres stati in singulis prytaneis æqualiter ferè inter se distantes, extraordinariarum pro rebus natis: illæ [?]ἐκκλησίαι, hæ [?]κατεκκλησίαι, aut [?]σύγκλητοι ἐκ-

page.notes: Greek words in the last lines are hard to read at the scan edge; the marked forms are uncertain. The hyphenated Greek word ἐκ- continues on the next page as κλησία (catchword). The word "εἰσαγ-γελίας" is split at the line end. The word "fœdera" may be "fædera" in the original; I read the ligature as printed.
